jobs.description:
Under the general direction of the Executive Director of Development, the Senior Director of Development (Sr. DoD) serves as a key member of UCLA Anderson's development team and directly supervises professional staff responsible for implementing and administering assigned fundraising programs. Leading the school's Major Giving team, the Sr. DoD designs and develops fundraising objectives and, through subordinate professional staff, implements and evaluates activities supporting established unit goals. The position selects, trains, directs, evaluates and motivates staff; coordinates work assignments and project priorities; and ensures accountability for assigned operational, financial and human resources. In partnership with the Executive Director of Development and the Senior Associate Dean of External Affairs, the Sr. DoD develops and executes short- and long-term fundraising strategies within established priorities to support the school's vision and strategic plan. The position participates in strategic planning, administers approved budget allocations and guides the preparation of fundraising materials, proposals and presentations. Applying full knowledge of the assigned fundraising area, the Sr. DoD interprets established policies and exercises judgment within defined procedures to resolve operational issues and recommend program improvements. Working collaboratively with colleagues across UCLA Anderson, UCLA External Affair and campus-wide as well as other internal/external constituents, the Sr. DoD coordinates fundraising efforts and supports staff in achieving established goals. With an emphasis on major gifts of $250,000 or more and endowment gifts of $350,000 or more, the position builds and maintains an assigned portfolio of donors and prospect and engages regularly with donors and volunteers to strengthen the school's major giving pipeline. This role offers an outstanding opportunity to apply leadership, communication and relationship-building skills to secure philanthropic support for academic programs, accomplished faculty and students from diverse backgrounds. As part of a school recognized for innovation in management education and research, the Sr. DoD advances UCLA Anderson's mission to develop transformative leaders who combine innovative problem-solving, technological and analytical fluency, and the interpersonal skills to inspire positive change. In addition, to establishing overall fundraising priorities for the Major Giving team, the Sr. DoD also oversees budget allocations, and serves as a delegated authority of the Executive Director and Senior Associate Dean as appropriate. This individual determines staff assignments and implementation methods within those parameters, consulting with the Executive Director on policy exceptions, additional resource needs and changes in program scope. In addition, the Sr. DoD serves as an advisor to the unit and administration on matters within the assigned area.

**Position Description**

The Managing Director, Direct Response serves as UNICEF USA's senior leader responsible for driving donor acquisition, retention, upgrade, and reactivation through offline direct response channels and the monthly giving program. Reporting directly to the Vice President, Donor Marketing & Journeys, this role leads UNICEF USA's direct response fundraising efforts and ensures that all offline campaigns, channel investments, vendor partnerships, and giving programs are strategically deployed, rigorously measured, and continuously optimized to support broader donor growth and revenue goals.

The Managing Director provides leadership across the full offline channel mix, including direct mail and telemarketing as the team's current active channels, with an eye toward evaluating and potentially expanding into additional offline channels such as face-to-face fundraising and other emerging offline opportunities as the program grows. This role provides senior oversight of the monthly giving program, managing a dedicated Manager of Monthly Giving who will handle day-to-day program management across both traditional direct response and digital channels, ensuring a coordinated and cohesive sustainer strategy regardless of channel. Additionally, the Managing Director oversees UNICEF USA's presence on third-party giving platforms, spanning both workplace giving and employer match programs as well as consumer-facing charitable giving aggregators where donors give to nonprofits through an intermediary platform.

This role works closely with cross-functional partners across Philanthropy, Finance, Technology, and Philanthropy Insight to ensure direct response programs align with broader donor engagement strategies and organizational priorities.

The Managing Director also plays an important role in shaping UNICEF USA's direct response capabilities, helping identify new channels, vendors, and performance approaches that strengthen the organization's long-term offline growth, and in managing and mentoring a team of direct response professionals.

**Channel Strategy & Oversight (40%)**

* Set the strategic direction for UNICEF USA's offline direct response program across all active and emerging channels, including direct mail and telemarketing, with the potential to expand into face-to-face fundraising and other offline channels over time
* Provide senior oversight of integrated multi-channel direct response campaigns that drive acquisition, retention, upgrade, and reactivation across mass market and leadership giving segments, with day-to-day execution managed by direct reports and vendor partners
* Guide campaign planning, segmentation strategy, and testing roadmaps, ensuring the team and agency partners are aligned on priorities and working toward clear, measurable goals

Review and approve campaign strategies, creative briefs, and performance recommendations brought forward by the team and agency partners, providing strategic guidance and direction rather than driving execution directly

**Vendor & Agency Management (15%)**

* Serve as the primary relationship lead for all direct response agency partners and vendors, including direct mail agencies, telemarketing vendors, and fulfillment partners
* Establish performance benchmarks and accountability frameworks for all vendor relationships, ensuring partners are delivering against agreed targets and continuously improving
* Lead regular performance reviews and planning sessions with vendor partners and internal stakeholders
Manage vendor contracts, SOWs, and budget allocations in partnership with Finance and Legal

  

**Monthly Giving Program (15%)**

* Provide senior oversight of UNICEF USA's monthly giving program, managing a dedicated Manager of Monthly Giving responsible for day-to-day program management across direct response and digital channels
* Set strategic direction for sustainer acquisition, upgrade, retention, save, and reactivation efforts, ensuring the program is coordinated and cohesive across all touchpoints
Set and track KPIs for monthly giving program health, including retention rate, average gift, and net sustainer growth

  

**Team Leadership (10%)**

* Manage and mentor a team of direct response professionals, providing day-to-day direction, support, and accountability
* Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and data-driven decision making across the direct response team
Invest in the professional development and growth of team members, helping them build skills and advance their careers over time

  

**Performance, Analytics & Optimization (5%)**

* Translate business goals into actionable campaign and channel strategies with measurable outcomes tied to revenue, donor file growth, retention, and long-term donor value
* Lead test-and-learn strategy across all direct response channels, applying rigorous testing methodologies to continuously optimize channel mix, messaging, offer strategy, and segmentation
* Develop and own channel-level dashboards and performance reports in collaboration with Philanthropy Insight and Technology
Utilize advanced segmentation and data modeling to identify the highest-potential audiences for each channel and optimize investment allocation accordingly

**Performance, Analytics & Optimization (5%)**

* Strengthen operational clarity around campaign development, performance monitoring, and optimization cycles

jobs.description:
**Company Description**

KIPP New Jersey is part of the nationally recognized “Knowledge Is Power Program” network of free, open-enrollment, college-preparatory public schools dedicated to preparing students for success in college and in life. In 2002, KIPP New Jersey first opened its doors in Newark’s South Ward as a single class of 80 fifth graders and has since grown to educate students in grades K-12 across 18 schools in Newark, Camden, and Paterson. More than 90% of KIPP New Jersey students currently qualify for free or reduced meals.

 **Job Description**

The Managing Director of School Operations for High Schools (HS MDSO) owns operational excellence at our two Newark high schools. Our high schools, including their operations, are not yet where our students need them to be. This role exists to change that. The HS MDSO sets an uncompromising bar for what excellent high school operations look like, models it personally, and demands it from every Director of Campus Operations (DCO) and ops team they lead.

The role starts with improving and supporting the schools we have: attendance, enrollment and 8th-to-9th persistence, safe and beautiful buildings, and systems that protect every instructional minute. It grows into building the operational standard that defines a KIPP Newark high school.

The HS MDSO reports to the Managing Director of Operations (MDO) and works in close partnership with the Managing Director of High Schools, who leads academic outcomes for the same schools. Academics and operations work toward one shared set of goals for the same students.

**Scope of Responsibility**

* **Newark high schools:** Direct management of the DCOs at our two Newark high schools; be accountable, jointly with each School Leader, for their success and the performance of their ops teams.
* **High school leadership:** Operations partner to the Managing Director of High Schools and the high school School Leaders.
* **Regional and network:** Works with Newark regional and network operations teams to set, standardize, and improve high school operational systems.

**Priorities**

**Priority 1: Raise the bar on high school operations now**

*This is the first job and the one that matters most in year one. Every system in both buildings should be joyful, safe, and efficient, and should protect instructional time.*

* Name the non-negotiables for high school operations, set clear expectations and owners for every system and project, and hold the line.
* Inspect what we expect. Walk systems (such as arrival, dismissal, meals, attendance, and transitions) with each DCO before the year begins and throughout it, confirming that execution matches design, and coach in real time.
* Run monthly audits of materials and systems and quarterly reviews to find what broke down, what can be streamlined, and where instructional minutes are being lost.
* Set and hold the expectation of a beautiful school: clean, orderly, bright spaces that tell students and staff they are valued here.
* Close every loop. Follow problems through to real resolution, name whether they are school, regional, or network problems, and bring in the right people.

**Priority 2: Coach and develop DCOs to an excellent bar**

*Our DCOs and ops teams get better because this person coaches them directly, gives frank feedback, and models what excellent looks like.*

* Hold weekly one-on-ones with each DCO and weekly/bi-weekly observations of each school's operational systems, processes, and meetings.
* Coach the coach: observe how DCOs lead their teams, give feedback on the questions they ask, and push them to see around corners.
* Address underperformance directly and constructively, as soon as it appears.
* Review DCO project plans (state testing, events, safety) against a clear bar before execution, and lead debriefs and after-action reviews that lead to fast iteration.
* Lead tabletop exercises on emergencies and high-stakes days so every ops leader has answered "what happens if \_\_\_" before it happens.
* Design professional development pathways for every school ops role so that high-performing ops teams exist in both schools, and step in to serve in a school operations capacity when coverage is needed.

**Priority 3: Drive the operational outcomes that matter for high school students**

**Job Description**

About the Agency:
  
  
The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.
  
As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.
  
  
Your Team:
  
  
The Office of Neighborhood Strategies (ONS) is charged with ensuring that HPD’s development and preservation efforts are guided by meaningful community engagement and coordinated with public investments in infrastructure and services, as put forth in the Mayor’s Housing Plan.
  
ONS is composed of two divisions and a cross-divisional unit reporting to the Associate Commissioner:
  

* The Division of Planning and Predevelopment (P&P) is central to developing and managing HPD's housing production pipeline from project proposal phases through the land use review and entitlement process, to ensure that HPD's investments contribute to building strong, healthy, resilient neighborhoods in all five boroughs. The advertised position is a member of this division.
* The Division of Neighborhood Development & Stabilization (ND&S) leads the agency's commitment to neighborhood planning and strategic preservation through engagement with tenants, landlords, community leaders, and neighborhood stakeholders as we work to enable strong and healthy neighborhoods anchored by affordable housing.
* The Strategic Initiatives Unit (SIU) leads special ONS initiatives and provides essential technical, planning, and policy support to staff and the Deputy Commissioner of Neighborhood Strategies.

  
Your Impact:
  
  
As the Executive Director of Borough Planning, you will advance HPD’s affordable housing mission by providing strategic and technical expertise and guidance to borough planning units within ONS. You will help to advance the creation of HPD’s new construction pre-development pipeline resulting in the creation of thousands of homes, and new community and retail opportunities. The Executive Director of Borough Planning reports to the Assistant Commissioner for Planning and Predevelopment.
  
This role will support the Mamdani Administration’s Streamlining Procedures to Expedite Equitable Development (“SPEED”) initiative, a sweeping set of reforms to deliver affordable housing faster across New York City.
  
  
Your Role:
  
  
The Executive Director of Borough Planning will oversee and manage four Borough Planning teams (~16 staff) to advance affordable housing and community development projects throughout the five boroughs. Primary roles include creation and maintenance of standard practices related to public engagement, ensuring affordable housing projects on City-owned land move expeditiously and efficiently through engagement and entitlements processes, intra- and inter-agency coordination, coaching and mentoring borough directors, and helping represent the agency in various aspects of projects, including in high-profile public-private planning and development processes, interagency initiatives, and in meetings with elected officials.
  
Your Responsibilities:
  
Under the supervision of the Assistant Commissioner for Planning and Predevelopment, the Executive Director of Borough Planning acts as a bridge between borough planning teams and ONS and agency leadership, helps institute and maintain standards across borough planning units, and provides coaching and mentorship to borough teams. Specifically, you will be expected to:
  
  
Planning and Project Management
  

* Work closely with borough directors in their review of HPD’s land use and other entitlement applications such as the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), Expedited Land Use Review Procedure (ELURP) and UDAAP applications. Ensure consistency and coach borough teams on best practices for producing materials prior to advancing them for review.
* Coordinate with ED of Land Use and Resiliency planning to prioritize projects for review.
* Help represent the borough teams in all aspects of large-scale planning and development projects, including neighborhood planning.
* In collaboration with other teams, and Assistant Commissioner as appropriate, identify and elevate political, policy, and programmatic flags on borough team projects to ONS leadership and provide recommendations for resolution, and aid Assistant Commissioner in analyzing and troubleshooting persistent or complex policy, planning, or technical issues.
* Collaborate with borough directors on strategy to successfully advance projects and across portfolios and advise Assistant Commissioner.

Unit Operations
